jordan_acme: hitting 403s intermittently from our app after we switched to PrivateLink earlier today. Some requests succeed, others fail with 403 from /v1/generate. No changes on our side. 

alex (support): sorry about that — can you paste a failing curl and the exact Host you hit? are you going through a proxy or egress appliance? :thinking_face: 

jordan_acme: curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' --data '{"prompt":"hi"}'

*response:* 
HTTP/2 403
content-type: application/json
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"access denied"}

We have an outbound squid proxy + egress firewall. No auth changes. 

alex (support): thanks. can you also run a DNS check from the host that's failing? e.g. dig +short api.redwood.example.com && curl --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:<ip-from-dig> -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

jordan_acme: ok running now — dig returns: 
10.12.5.43 
172.65.210.12 

curl --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.12.5.43 -v ... -> 200
curl --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:172.65.210.12 -v ... -> 403

So looks like some requests go to the private VPCE IP (10.12.5.43) and others hit a public IP and 403. Not all AZs see the private mapping. 

priya (eng-infra): interesting — that suggests split-horizon PHZ not associated to all subnets/route53 resolver rules. which AZ are your failing hosts in? any NAT/proxy sitting in a different AZ? 

jordan_acme: failing hosts mostly in us-east-1a and our proxy pool is in us-east-1b. 

priya (eng-infra): another possibility: VPCE DNS options need enableDnsHostnames/enableDnsSupport and the Private Hosted Zone must be associated with the VPCs that host the clients. please run: 

aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0abc1234 --region us-east-1 

and also check VPC Endpoint DNS entries: 

# from an EC2 in the same subnet
getent hosts api.redwood.example.com

if it returns public IP from some instances that's the root cause.

jordan_acme: list-hosted-zones-by-vpc returns nothing for vpc-0abc1234 in us-east-1a. Oops. Looks like the PHZ association never completed for that VPC/subnet during cutover. 

alex (support): that would explain split behavior. Requests that resolve to public IPs go out over internet (and your firewall/proxy drops or returns 403). Requests resolving to vpce private IP hit the PrivateLink and succeed. 

dan (eng-sre): quick mitigation: associate the PHZ to the missing VPCs/azs OR add a conditional route so your proxy performs DNS sinkhole to VPCE IPs. Also verify your outbound allowlist doesn't block the VPCE IP range. run these: 

aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0abc1234

# then on a host that failed, run
getent hosts api.redwood.example.com && curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

priya (eng-infra): FYI if you can't change PHZ right away, a quick stopgap is to pin via /etc/hosts for the proxy box to the VPCE IPs for api.redwood.example.com (not ideal but works for short term). also confirm your proxy preserves TLS SNI — some appliances terminate TLS and re-mint certs which can cause 403s if Host header doesn't match. 

jordan_acme: associating PHZ worked, tested from one host in us-east-1a: getent returns 10.12.5.43 and curl returns 200 consistently now. Rolling out to proxies. Huge thanks. :tada: 

alex (support): glad that fixed it. i'll keep the ticket open for a day to watch for recurrence. can you also check your egress allowlist to ensure the VPCE CIDR is allowed (some teams whitelist public IP ranges only)? 

jordan_acme: will do. quick note for our runbook: after PrivateLink cutover ensure PHZ associations across all VPCs and AZ-level proxy pools. saving this thread. :memo: 

ops-bot: Incident auto-close scheduled in 24h unless updated. :bell: 

alex (support): closing loop — root cause: missing Route53 Private Hosted Zone association for one VPC/subnet causing DNS to sometimes resolve to public IPs. secondary contributing factor: proxy/egress allowed only public IPs which returned 403s. resolution: associate PHZ + update proxy allowlist.

dan (eng-sre): adding to infra checklist so future PrivateLink cutovers validate PHZ associations & run getent hosts from each AZ/proxy pool.

jordan_acme: thanks everyone, great support.
